# Your Song: how this page was made

**Live page:** https://brendansudol.github.io/setlist/your-song/

[`index.html`](index.html) is a one-file explainer for the fourteen
fretting-hand shapes in the intro and verse of a fingerstyle arrangement of
"Your Song", worked out from a YouTube guitar lesson. It is generated by
[`build.py`](build.py). Tapping any timestamp plays that moment of the lesson
in a YouTube player that stays on screen. This file records where the content
came from, how the page was produced, and what is and is not certain.

## Source

| | |
|---|---|
| Video | [Your Song by Elton John - Fingerstyle Guitar Lesson](https://youtu.be/o3AstcWl7E8) |
| Channel | Six String Fingerpicking |
| Length | 23:27 |
| Covers | Intro and verse (both halves). The instructor says the rest of the lesson is on his website. |
| Tuning | Standard |
| Capo | Fret 2 in the lesson. The instructor calls it optional and says fret 1 matches the original. |

Every chord name and fret number on the page is **counted from the capo**,
because that is how the lesson names things ("as if there were no capo at
all").

## Who made it

Claude (Anthropic's AI model) produced the page in one working session, right
after packaging the first song in this repository.

## The prompt

The session already held the handoff note for
[The Heart of Life](../heart-of-life/README.md), which describes the pipeline
and its rules. The whole request for this page was:

> now do the same for https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=o3AstcWl7E8&t=625s

The `t=625s` in the link is 10:25, where the instructor replays line 1 of the
verse and carries on into line 2. The page links to that moment from the chord
map.

## Process

1. **Facts about the video.** The video was opened in Chrome. Title, channel,
   length and the chapter list in the description were read from
   `window.ytInitialPlayerResponse`.
2. **Transcript.** The "Show transcript" panel was opened and its 199 segments
   read from the page. The transcript gives the chord names and most of the
   frets and strings, because the instructor says them out loud.
3. **Frames to confirm each shape.** For each chord the video was paused at
   one or more moments and the fretting hand inspected at full 1080p
   resolution. Inlays and fret wires were counted from the capo to read the
   fret; the string was read from where the fingertip lands.
4. **Data, then a generator.** The shapes went into `build.py` as data. The
   script checks every shape before writing any HTML (see below), then draws
   all the diagrams as inline SVG.
5. **Layout check.** The page was rendered at 390px wide in headless Chrome,
   in light and dark mode, section by section.

### Getting frames from a background tab

Two things were different from the first song and are worth knowing for next
time.

- **Chrome would not load the video.** The automation tab was never visible,
  and Chrome defers loading media in a tab that has never been shown and has
  never played anything. The fix was to play a silent, generated audio stream
  in the page first. After that the tab counts as having played media, and
  reloading the video through the player's own `loadVideoById` call worked.
- **Frames were read through a canvas.** Instead of scaling the `<video>`
  element with CSS, each frame was drawn onto a `<canvas>` with
  `drawImage(video, sx, sy, sw, sh, ...)`, cropping to the fretting hand. Four
  to six crops at different timestamps were tiled into one canvas, each
  labelled with its time, and the canvas was screenshotted. That gives several
  moments per screenshot at native resolution.

The frames and the transcript were working material only. Neither is in this
repository or on the page.

## How sure each part is

- **Confirmed by both the transcript and the frames:** the chord order, the
  capo position, and the frets and strings of thirteen of the fourteen shapes.
- **Partly confirmed: G.** The frames clearly show the middle finger on the
  low E string at fret 3 and the index at fret 2. The ring and pinky on the
  top two strings could not be read with confidence from the camera angle, and
  the lesson only says "G". The diagram shows the usual four-finger G and the
  page says so on the card.
- **Finger numbers.** Taken from the video where a frame shows them clearly
  (Gmaj7, the thumb on Bm/G# and G6) or the instructor says them (A/C#).
  Otherwise they are the usual fingering for the shape. The page states this.
- **Bar lengths.** The lesson says D and Gmaj7 make up the first bar and
  A/C# and F#m7 the second. The page repeats only that, and otherwise lists
  the chords in order without claiming bar counts.

## Checks built into the generator

`build.py` refuses to write the page unless, for every shape:

- the notes produced by its strings and frets (standard tuning, counted from
  the capo) match the expected note list exactly;
- every note belongs to the chord the shape is named after;
- the lowest played string gives the expected bass note;
- every fretted string has a finger, and no open or unplayed string does;
- any barre lies on played strings and uses one finger;
- the shape fits in a four-fret diagram.

It also checks that every chord in the three sequences exists, that every
shape is used at least once, and that all timestamps fall inside the video.

After the build, a separate pass confirmed that every in-page link has a
target and that the HTML tags balance.

## Rules the page follows

The same rules as the first song:

- **No video frames.** Diagrams are original drawings, and every shape links
  to its moment in the video.
- **No lyrics, and no note-by-note melody or TAB.** This matters more here
  than for the first song, because the lesson is a full arrangement in which
  every bar has its own picking. The page deliberately stops at the shapes,
  the chord order, where the bass note is, and five single reaches. The
  picking is pointed to, not written out.
- **Fingering is labelled honestly**, as described above.

The page was first built with a fourth rule, no embedded player, inherited
from a host that blocked iframes. That rule has been dropped; see the next
section. The page is still one file and still contains no footage.

## The docked player

Added after the page was first published. The player was tried on
[All The Small Things](../all-the-small-things/README.md#the-docked-player)
first, and the request that brought it here was:

> yes, push it live and can we also incorporate for the other songs too

It is the same player: the styles, markup and script were copied from that
song's `build.py` into this one, and that write-up describes how it behaves
at each window width, the speed and loop buttons, and the fallback to plain
links. What is specific to this page:

- **37 timestamps play in the page:** the fourteen cards, the four parts of
  the chord map, the five reaches, the ten chapters and the four shortcuts.
- **The shortcuts** beside the video on a wider window are the four parts of
  the chord map: Intro, Verse line 1, Verse line 2 and the second half of the
  verse. They come from `PARTS` in `build.py`.
- **Checked** in a desktop browser at 1152 by 630, 900 by 700 and 375 by 812:
  a tap plays the right moment of the right video, the shortcuts, speed and
  loop work, a chord tapped in the map lands in view, and closing the video
  leaves the page where it was. It was not tested on a real phone.

## Design

Same layout and type as the first song. What changed:

- **Four shape families instead of three**, so there is a fourth colour:
  open chords, the Bm barre shape (Bm, Bm/A, Bm/G#, Em), the full barre at
  fret 2 (F#m7, F#7), and small shapes over a bass note (G/D, A/D, Gmaj7, G6).
  Colour still means the family and nothing else.
- **A chord map in four parts** replaces the single eight-bar loop.
- **A bass-note map replaces the picking grid.** There is no single pattern to
  draw, so the figure shows which string and fret the thumb starts on for each
  verse chord. It also makes the descending bass under the Bm shape visible.
- **The thick top line of a diagram is the capo**, and it is labelled.

## Rebuilding

```bash
python3 your-song/build.py
```

Standard library only. Edit the data at the top of `build.py`, not
`index.html`; the next build overwrites the HTML.

## What is not in this repository

- The transcript and the frames used to confirm the shapes.
- Any part of the song after the verse. It is not in this video.
